_comment: Canonical character and system voice lines for the game. Narration is excluded because it is audiobook-only. `audio` points at the same clip the audiobook plays: one generated line, used in both places.

lines.text: Come on. What are you doing?
I've got something weird on my computer. It tripped a security alarm.
I think somebody's in the system.
No. That's why I'm calling the smarter scientist.
Can you come take a look?
Please tell me you didn't break something.
You called me in here to admit that?
I was reviewing yesterday's test results.
I got an unauthorized access warning. I checked the network monitor and saw a connection I didn't recognize, but it disappeared before I could trace it.
You know, you're supposed to be resting.
No. You're the one I found asleep at a laboratory terminal.
Lately the baby seems to think eleven at night is morning.
Being thirty-two weeks pregnant does not mean made of glass.
It means you're carrying something considerably more important than this laboratory.
Warning. array power above standby threshold.
Control, this is Bennett. Shut down power to TOMBS.
Jack, we were about to call you. We're seeing a massive draw from your building.
Yesterday's full test didn't use half that.
Possible network intrusion. Cut external access to the laboratory and disconnect TOMBS from the island grid.
Then where is it getting the power?
Then we'll do it the old-fashioned way.
I didn't do it the first time.
That's what I want to know.
Lena, keep the laboratory isolated. Don't sound a settlement alarm yet.
No. But I don't know what we'd be telling people to do, and I don't want anyone running toward whatever this is.
Quiet containment until we know the boundary.
If anything changes outside this building, call us.
Maybe good, or maybe everyone-inside-the-field-dies bad?
Come on. Give me manual control!
I'll try to interrupt the calculation.
I'm here. I don't think so.
Which means something is very wrong.
We've got power. Most systems are responding, but communications are down.
External. We can't reach anything beyond the settlement.
We think the developed zone was inside the boundary.
The system hid the final coordinates before activation.
We only confirmed the result afterward.
Lena, go to a window. Don't go outside.
There's a wall behind the east fence.
I was hoping you wouldn't say that.
Keep the night crew inside too. No general alarm yet. I don't want people pouring into the streets before we know what's out there.
Take it. I'll stay with Lena.
Doctor Bennett, this is Doctor Mercer. Did your lab just cause that vibration?
That is not the answer I wanted.
It's not the one I wanted to give.
Nothing serious. One patient woke up frightened, two nurses felt the floor move, and half my overnight staff are arguing about whether we had an earthquake.
Local sensors show no seismic event.
Then why am I looking at grass taller than the medical center?
Jack, I work nights. Looking outside occasionally is one of the perks.
We had a TOMBS boundary event. The developed settlement appears to have been reduced in scale relative to the surrounding island.
What do you need from medical?
For now, keep your overnight staff inside. Check backup power, medical gases, water pressure, and anything that crosses the edge of the developed zone. Don't wake patients unless you need to.
And when they wake on their own?
Lena says most of the developed zone still has power. Three localized faults, nothing catastrophic.
Unit Twelve, this is Bennett. Do not cross the end of the road. Turn around and return to the developed zone.
Doctor, I wasn't planning on crossing it.
Dirt. Grass. A lot of both.
And I think the dirt is higher than my vehicle.
Return to town. Quietly. Security personnel only at the perimeter until we know more.
We can't keep this quiet until morning.
But waking everyone right now could be worse.
Then we tell the people who need to know first. Medical. Utility. Security. Anyone already awake.
We give ourselves enough time to learn what we're waking them up to.
Could the sensors just be disconnected?
You found the intake, didn't you?
Same thing. Power conduit, water intake, and the old fiber trunk. Everything ends cleanly.
How much water is stored inside the settlement?
The tanks were designed as buffers, not as our only supply.
Give us the conservative number when you have it.
Please tell me that was something in your building.
Nobody goes outside the developed zone,
With your eyes open this time?
What are you going to tell them?
And don't promise them a reversal.
I should be able to reverse what it did.
That still isn't the same as knowing you can.

This is Doctor Jack Bennett from the TOMBS laboratory. Earlier tonight, the settlement experienced a TOMBS boundary event. Power, atmosphere, medical services, and most internal infrastructure remain operational.

We have confirmed that the developed settlement changed in scale relative to the surrounding island. If you are inside a residence or other secure building, remain there for now. Do not approach the outer edge of town and do not enter undeveloped terrain. Medical, utility, and security teams are operating normally.
We are investigating the cause and whether the event can be reversed. We will provide another update when we have verified information. If you have an emergency, use the normal emergency channels.
I hated every word of that.
Especially the part where I didn't say we'd fix it.
Then let's earn the right to say it later.
At current normal consumption, bad. With emergency restrictions, considerably less bad.
Several days before we have to start making uncomfortable decisions. Longer if we shut down nonessential industrial use and recycle aggressively.
No, you said you liked Doctor Mercer.
I can like two competent people in one night.
Security logged three vibrations since the last one. They don't match anything on the local seismic sensors.
Or whatever is causing them is.
Please tell me we're not using the phrase whatever is causing them in the next public announcement.
Like the security logs before activation.
It could delete logs if an administrator ordered it.
Then whoever did this had more than remote access.
Before either of you asks, yes, the station is staffed, yes, the grid is stable, and yes, I locked the door.
I was going to ask two of those.
It looks disappointingly normal for a machine that just ruined everyone's night.
Doctor Bennett, we have a perimeter team ready.
Visual inspection of the southern boundary.
Inside the developed zone only. They want to see where the road ends.
We are absolutely doing this again.
We don't know what's out there.
Which is why a scientist should be there.
You're thirty-two weeks pregnant, it's the middle of the night, and something outside town may be causing ground vibrations.
It wasn't easy. It was reasonable.
I'm uncomfortable with how suspicious you are of reasonable.
Take readings at the boundary. Air composition, temperature, pressure, particulates, radiation, anything the unit can measure.
Air is normal. Temperature difference is negligible. Pressure is normal.
My hand is still on our side.
You are genetically incapable of saying that reassuringly.
That doesn't make it less unpleasant.
I said I saw something that looked like thin legs.
For the record, I support running away from unidentified giant things.
Everything outside the boundary tested normal.
Normal atmosphere. Same composition, same pressure, same temperature within the sensor's tolerance.
Then physically, we can breathe out there.
Probably isn't going in the public announcement either.
Good. I wanted to make sure I was contributing.
It's the one I have right now.
Can you tell what they entered?
TOMBS wasn't simply told to make the settlement smaller.
It was given a target scale,
Meaning whoever did this chose how small?
That's what I'm trying to confirm.
If the transformation is uniform, an average adult here is somewhere around several millimeters tall.
Could the system have picked that number randomly?
Could it have been an accident?
The activation itself could have resulted from corrupted commands. But a specific target scale is different.
The boundary wasn't centered on TOMBS.
They knew what counted as developed infrastructure.
So someone prepared this three weeks ago?
Can you see who created it?
I'm asking why the computer thinks he did.
You were both at the community center.
